summary: Graham Mountain tower, first erected by NYSDEC on Pocotello Mountain (1930), moved to its present site in 1948; NHLR-registered 1995; not regularly staffed since 1989.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower with 7 by 7 foot steel cab
facts.status_note: The April 2021 FFLA newsletter describes footings and a lot of communications equipment on site; it is not a full inspection of the tower.

access.note: Access road off Mountain Road below Otisville usually has a secured gate; the Register says the land may be private. Based on Bob Spear's undated Register history notes; no current access rules found.

visit.trail_note: Park near the abandoned house described in the Register notes (there at one time) and walk about ten minutes, fairly level, to the road that leads to the tower. Check with NYSDEC before going; no source says whether climbing is allowed now.

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Tower erected on Pocatello Mountain (Sayers Hill) near Lake Pocatello; a Middletown newspaper reported it ready for inspection in August 1930. The Register gives no build year.
Dismantled and moved to a site nearby on Graham Mountain
Register visit note says the tower was not regularly staffed since 1989
Visit report dated July 29, 2004 by Bob Spear: tower needs paint; electronic sites encroaching; described as abandoned
April 2021 FFLA visit: footings look good, a lot of communications equipment, repairs likely only lumber replacement

notes_for_editor: Build year: the brief had none. The 1930 date rests on the Middletown Times Herald (Aug 1930) and the 1930 state annual report, both quoted on the Pocatello Mountain page of Forest Lookouts, plus the NHLR's statement that the tower was first erected on Pocotello Mountain. A Facebook group post dated the Pocatello tower 1930 but the page could not be read, so it is not cited. Access 'unknown' in the brief is replaced by 'restricted' from Bob Spear's undated Register history notes (gate and private-land remarks), which may be out of date. The brief's elevation (396.2 m) and OSM node were not read and are not used. Current climbability and the tower's present condition are not established by any source read. The April 2021 newsletter's 'Roosa Gap' paragraph about reopening refers to a different tower and is not applied to Graham.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register spells the mountain Pocotello and calls it Sayers Hill. The 1930 state annual report spells it Pocatello, and the 1930 Middletown newspaper places the tower at Sayer's Hill near Lake Pocatello. All refer to the same mountain.
